title: Kabin Buri Mountain-View Cafes 2026 — 8 Cafes on the Khao Yai Route
metaDesc: Our ranked pick of mountain- and rice-field-view cafes in Kabin Buri and along the Prachinburi-side road up to Khao Yai, Thailand. Real, open spots with areas, signature drinks and rough prices, drawn from genuine reviews.

h1:
Kabin Buri Mountain-View Cafes
On the Road Up to Khao Yai
intro: Kabin Buri is the Prachinburi-side gateway that climbs straight up toward Khao Yai, and the road there is dotted with cafes. Some look out onto a wall of mountains, others let you sit and watch green rice fields in the morning light. We picked 8 places that are genuinely open and come up often in reviews, with the area, signature drinks and rough prices for each.

blocks.html: If you drive in from Bangkok via the motorway and turn off into Kabin Buri, this is the shortcut up to Khao Yai that Prachinburi locals use all the time. The charm of the route is the cafes tucked between the rice paddies and the foot of the hills. Many open very early because they catch both the people topping up on coffee before the climb and the cycling crowd. We've ordered them by how worth-it the stop is, looking at the view, the menu and what real reviews say.

blocks.text: 8 mountain- and rice-field-view cafes worth a stop

items.name: Compass Coffee Roasters (Kabin Buri)
items.blurb: A specialty cafe right on Route 304 as you come into Kabin Buri town, with its own roaster on display out front, high ceilings and plenty of seating. Reviewers keep mentioning the Gravity (a dirty-style double shot), the matcha and the carrot cake. A solid place to fuel up on coffee before the climb to Khao Yai.
items.meta: Kabin Buri old town · on Route 304

items.name: Noen Homme Cafe (Noen Hom)
items.blurb: Sits near the foot of the Khao Yai road on the Noen Hom side, shaded by big trees, with an earthen house and several photo corners. It opens very early, so cyclists climbing the hill love stopping here to recharge. There are both indoor and outdoor zones.
items.meta: Noen Hom · near the Khao Yai turnoff

items.name: Myrrh. Cafe
items.blurb: A minimal, all-white cafe with an open outlook onto Khao Yai and Khao E-Toh as a backdrop. Pets are welcome and there are corners for working too. Best for photos with the mountains on a clear morning.
items.meta: Noen Hom · next to Myrrh Resort

items.name: Bliss & Bloom Cafe (Thap Lan)
items.blurb: Inside The Verona project in the Thap Lan area, with a view of the hills and flower fields and a European-style fit-out. Good for anyone who likes a garden atmosphere and lots of photo corners. The blueberry cheesecake gets a lot of mentions.

items.name: Baan Chang Cafe
items.blurb: The draw here is the easy-on-the-eyes view of green rice fields. There's an EV charging point and the menu is more substantial than most, with pizza, steak and bingsu. Good for a lunch stop where you settle in for a while.

items.name: De Nadi Casa & Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe on Route 304 with a minimal-meets-vintage fit-out. The selling points are single-origin coffee and croissants, and it stays open into the evening, making it a good stop on the way back from Khao Yai.

items.name: Mo Garden & Cafe
items.blurb: A garden cafe in Kabin Buri town with a shady, leafy setting that's comfortable to sit in. A handy mid-day break if you don't want to drive out far, and a place locals drop by regularly.

items.name: Little House Cafe
items.blurb: A homey roadside cafe with homemade bakery, steak and one-plate dishes, plus cats to play with. It opens early, from seven, so it's good for a light breakfast before you carry on.

blocks.title: When to go
blocks.html: The mountain views are clearest in the morning once the sky opens up, especially in the cool season (Nov–Feb). The rice fields are greenest from the rainy season into early winter. If you're set on photos with the mountains as a backdrop, go before 10am for nicer light and fewer people than in the afternoon.

If you've got half a day, try lining the cafes up along one route so you're not doubling back. Below is a rough plan that starts in Kabin Buri town and works its way up toward Noen Hom and the Khao Yai turnoff.

blocks.label: Morning half-day
blocks.title: Kabin Buri → Noen Hom → Khao Yai turnoff

items.activity: Start at Compass Coffee Roasters for your first cup and something sweet
items.note: Come a little early while it's still quiet so you can shoot the roaster easily

items.activity: Drive up toward Noen Hom and stop at Myrrh. Cafe for photos with Khao Yai and Khao E-Toh
items.note: The sky is still clear, so the mountains are at their sharpest now

items.activity: Stop at Noen Homme Cafe before the climb and take a break over a cold drink
items.note: If you're heading on up to Khao Yai, this is the spot to recharge before the climb

items.activity: Finish with lunch at Baan Chang Cafe looking out over the rice fields
items.note: The mains are more substantial here; once you're full, decide whether to head up the mountain or back to town

blocks.text: Mountain view or rice-field view — which to pick

items: Want a wall of mountains as a backdrop — go for the Noen Hom–Khao Yai turnoff side, like Myrrh. and Noen Homme, where Khao Yai and Khao E-Toh are clearly in view
Want easy green rice fields — pick Baan Chang, where you can sit and watch the paddies for ages; best from the rainy season into early winter
Want serious coffee — Compass Coffee Roasters and De Nadi focus on the beans and the brew more than the view
Bringing pets or family — Myrrh. is pet-friendly, while Mo Garden and Little House have an easygoing feel that works with kids

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: A lot of these are small cafes that open and close depending on the day, and some are shut on weekdays. Before you set off, check the shop's page for that day, and bring some cash — a few of the smaller places only take bank transfers, or the signal isn't great near the foot of the hills.

faq.q: Which Kabin Buri cafe has the best mountain view?
faq.a: If you want Khao Yai and Khao E-Toh as a backdrop, Myrrh. Cafe and Noen Homme Cafe on the Noen Hom–turnoff side do it well. On a clear morning is when you'll see the mountains most sharply.

faq.q: Which cafe should I go to for a rice-field view?
faq.a: Baan Chang Cafe is the spot to sit and watch green rice fields for a long stretch, with an EV charger and proper mains, so it's good for a lunch stop. The paddies are greenest from the rainy season into early winter.

faq.q: Can I stop at cafes on the route from Kabin Buri up to Khao Yai?
faq.a: Yes. The Prachinburi side goes up to Khao Yai via Noen Hom, and along the way there are several cafes like Compass, Myrrh. and Noen Homme, easy stops to top up on coffee before the climb.

faq.q: Roughly how much do cafes around here cost?
faq.a: Most drinks run about THB 60–150. At specialty spots like Compass a hot latte starts around THB 70. If you add a main dish or cake, expect roughly THB 120–280 per person.

faq.q: What time of day should I go?
faq.a: Morning to late morning is best — the mountain views are clear and it's quieter than the afternoon. Many cafes open very early to catch the cyclists climbing the hill. If you're going in the late afternoon, check the closing time first.
